cases.diagnostic: The larger support preserves the same solid spoon, but it remains at the liquid surface without a visibly lifted or contained payload.
The enlarged support does not repair the melted blade/payload region or restore distinct supported grains.

The motion-union projection retains exactly two separated chopsticks contacting a lifted bowl-connected noodle. The noodle remains soft/ghosted and the support is post-hoc and broader than the formal final edit region, so this is diagnostic topology recovery rather than a reported success.
The larger support retains one solid metal utensil but does not produce a four-tine fork or a readable spaghetti twirl.

decision: The full motion union is too broad for formal use, but it confirms that final support mismatch is the dominant projected-output failure for ramen only. A prospective follow-up should use a fixed narrow final-geometry tolerance corridor and validate it on a new seed or held-out case. Soup, rice, and pasta still require payload/utensil-head appearance improvements.
